## Description

Track returns of a predefined set of investable factor portfolios or liquid factor proxies, rank the factors by trailing performance over a fixed lookback (for example, 6–12 months), and tilt toward the strongest factors at a scheduled rebalance. A long-only top-k allocation with portfolio-level risk limits is a practical baseline; compare it with equal-weight and static factor allocations.

## Where it may fit

May benefit when factor returns persist; can struggle when factor leadership reverses or factor autocorrelation breaks down.

## Vehicles

Investable factor ETFs or transparent long-only factor portfolios; alternatively academic factor-return series for research only.

## Required data

Point-in-time monthly factor returns or investable proxy returns, benchmark returns, expense ratios, turnover, price history, and correlations across factors.

## Caveats

Published findings are mixed: some research documents factor momentum while other work finds weak effects across many individual factors and no consistent outperformance versus corresponding long-only strategies. Results depend on which factors, construction, proxies, lookbacks, and rebalance frequency are chosen. Factor-return data may not be directly investable; test actual vehicle costs and tracking error.

- **Reference review:** Multiple research references added; candidate not independently backtested; evidence mixed. — The cited 2023 Review of Financial Studies paper examines factor momentum; the 2022 Financial Review paper questions its strength and finds that strategies did not outperform corresponding long-only portfolios in its samples; the 2025 international study reports further cross-market evidence with methodological caveats.
- **Metadata alignment:** New candidate; define an investable factor universe, return history, risk scaling, rebalance dates, and benchmark before implementation.
